p: One of the joys of Eureka! on the Wirral is that the rest of the peninsula is so easy to tack on. Follow the promenade north and you'll eventually reach New Brighton, where Fort Perch Rock stands guard at the mouth of the Mersey. The sandstone fort was built in the 1820s to protect the port of Liverpool, and it's a striking sight at high tide when the water swirls round its base.

Inland, Birkenhead Park is well worth a detour. Opened in 1847, it's widely regarded as the first publicly funded park in Britain, and its design is said to have inspired New York's Central Park. There are lakes, bridges and wide lawns for a run-around, plus a visitor centre and café.

Head to the far west of the Wirral and West Kirby offers a marine lake and views out to the Hilbre Islands. You can walk out to them across the sands at low tide, but only with careful planning around the tide times, as the water comes in fast and people do get caught out.

Back at Eureka!, a little tip for families with a wide spread of ages: let the older kids pick one zone and the younger ones pick the next, swapping as you go. It keeps everyone happy and stops anyone sulking by the exit. Pack a spare top for younger children if they're the type to get stuck into anything wet or messy, and leave time for the gift shop, because you probably won't escape it. Proper Wirral day, that.
